title: Dimensional Modeling: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Measure Or Context | eight columns of a raw sales export sorted into measures, dimension keys, degenerate dimensions and attributes that wandered onto the fact, plus the same entity in two roles | facts are what you measure and dimensions are what you slice by, and both are roles determined by the business process rather than properties of a table

2. What Sums, What Does Not | order revenue, daily balance and conversion rate each summed across entities and across time, with sliders showing why averaging two stored rates gives the wrong combined rate | additive sums everywhere, semi-additive sums across entities but not time, and a stored ratio destroys the denominator weight no downstream query can recover

3. Declare The Grain | five candidate grain statements tested against the data, showing which key survives and which questions each grain can still answer | grain must be precise enough to test, atomic grain preserves the questions you have not thought of yet, and a snapshot grain needs both entity and time

4. Mixed Grain Overcounts | an order-level shipping cost repeated on every line with a slider for line count, plus the promotions many-to-many join and three repairs | an order-level measure on a line-level row overcounts by the line count, so the multiplier differs per order and no single scale factor reveals it

5. Star Or Snowflake | five considerations compared under both shapes, from join hops and compressed storage to shared hierarchies and many-to-many membership | star wins on usability and compression, snowflake wins on independent governance and genuine structure, and neither shape gives you history
